title: Statewide residential rent increase cap
requirement: For covered residential rental property, an owner may not increase rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the applicable cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower. If the same tenant remains in the unit, rent may not be increased in more than two increments during that 12-month period.
key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%; no more than two increases in 12 months for same tenant

title: Statewide just-cause eviction protections for residential tenancies
requirement: After the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential rental for 12 months, the owner may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice; if additional adult tenants join, protection applies when all tenants have 12 months or one has 24 months. For no-fault terminations, the owner must provide relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver equal to one month’s rent, and curable lease violations require a chance to cure first.

title: California residential security deposit limits and return rules
requirement: For residential rentals, a landlord generally may not demand or receive a security deposit greater than one month’s rent, must use it only for authorized purposes such as unpaid rent, tenant-caused damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and necessary cleaning, and must return the remainder with an itemized statement no later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates. Tenants may request an initial inspection before move-out, and bad-faith retention or claims against the deposit can expose the landlord to statutory damages.
